\[
x_*=A^{-1}b,\qquad r_k=b-Ax_k,\qquad \|v\|_A=(v^\top Av)^{1/2}.
\]
If \(r_k=0\), terminate. Otherwise, set
\[
\mathcal K_s(A,r_k)=\operatorname{span}\{r_k,Ar_k,\ldots,A^{s-1}r_k\}

\[
y_k=\frac{r_k}{\|r_k\|_2},\qquad \|v\|_2=(v^\top v)^{1/2}.

\beta(y)=\|q_y(A)y\|_2.

On a nonterminating orbit, the support has more than \(s\) nodes and \(\beta>0\). The actual residual-direction update is
\[
T(y)=(-1)^s\,q_y(A)y/\beta(y).

This follows from the minimizer’s residual orthogonality and the residual polynomial’s normalization at zero.

\[

\langle y,T^2y\rangle=\frac{\beta(y)}{\beta(Ty)},

\]

Here \(q(z)=z-\mu\), \(h=V\), the spectral variance. Its increase is

\]

\[
L_\beta=\log w_\beta+\sum_{i=1}^4\ell_i(\beta)\log w_i,
\]
where \(\ell_i\) are the core Lagrange polynomials. Polynomial BV and interpolation give eventual monotonicity:
\[
L_{\beta,k+2}-L_{\beta,k}
=-2\log(h_kh_{k+1}/H^2)+O((H-h_k)^2)\ge0.
\]
For \(\beta\) in either spectral band, exactly one core interpolation coefficient is negative. Since \(w_\beta\to0\), the entropy inequality forces that particular core weight to zero—contradicting a four-node union of limiting supports.

\[

\]
With \(R=\zeta-\eta\), exact scalar identities give
\[
R_{\rm next}=R+R^2A,\qquad
\zeta_{\rm next}-\zeta=C R_{\rm next},
\]
where \(A\) is bounded and \(C\ge0\) is bounded uniformly, including limiting endpoints. Exponentially small external perturbations are handled by an integrating-factor argument: either \(R\) has eventual fixed sign or is exponentially small. A useful general identity comes from \(qM=aP+t\):

\]

 # Compression proof for the interlacing polynomial B

Let n=2s, let y0,y1,y2 be three successive normalized residuals in the sign convention y1=q(A)y0/sqrt(h), y2=qnext(A)y1/sqrt(hnext) (the harmless common (-1)^s factors do not change spaces), and let P(z)=prod_i(z-lambda_i). Let M,Mnext,Mnextnext be their Stieltjes numerators. Divide qM=aP+t and qnext Mnext=anext P+tnext. Then Mnext=q t/h and a tnext-anext t=q B, where deg B<=s-2 and its leading coefficient is K=hnext-h>=0.

Suppose K>0. Put F=q qnext and w_i=y0_i^2. Orthogonality gives E_w F=h, E_w F^2=h hnext. Define S(z)=E_w[1/(z-lambda)], U(z)=E_w[F/(z-lambda)], V(z)=E_w[F^2/(z-lambda)]. Since (qnext(z)-qnext(lambda))/(z-lambda) has degree s-1 in lambda,
 U(z)=qnext(z)t(z)/P(z),
 V(z)=h qnext(z)tnext(z)/P(z).
Consequently
 S(z)V(z)-U(z)^2 = h qnext(z) B(z)/P(z).

The left side is det(X^T(zI-A)^(-1)X), where X has columns y0 and F(A)y0. By the compression determinant identity,
 P(z) det(X^T(zI-A)^(-1)X)=det(X^TX) det(zI-A_C),
where C=span{y0,F(A)y0}^perp=span{y0,y2}^perp and A_C denotes orthogonal compression. Here det(X^TX)=hK. Thus
 det(zI-A_C)=qnext(z) B(z)/K.

The subspace K_s(A,y1) lies in C: y2 is orthogonal to it by the minimization, and y0 is orthogonal to it by symmetry of A and the previous minimization. It is invariant under A_C, because A^s y1 belongs to K_s(A,y1)+span{y2}. Its characteristic polynomial for the compressed operator is qnext. Hence B/K is the characteristic polynomial of the compression to
 W=(K_s(A,y1)+span{y0,y2})^perp.

Now L=(K_s(A,y1)+span{y2})^perp has dimension s-1. The same invariant-subspace argument inside y2^perp shows that its compression has characteristic polynomial tnext/hnext. Moreover W is a codimension-one subspace of L, since K>0 means y0,y2 independent. Cauchy interlacing therefore proves that the s-2 roots of B interlace the s-1 roots of tnext. In particular, for s=3 the unique root of B lies between the two NEW Dirichlet poles. For s=2, B=K is positive constant.

The same proof works for general n, with deg B=n-s-2, dim L=n-s-1. It does not itself solve the extra-mode issue, since the poles corresponding to the limiting core need not be the outermost poles of tnext.


### experiments/e4/agent3_s3_global_cases.md 
 # s=3 global case reduction: proved cases and precise remaining step

Notation follows agent3_global_reduction.md and agent1_global_polynomial_proof.md. The even and odd monic cubics converge with bounded total variation to q,r; H=lim h>0; Q=qr. After discarding a finite initial segment all retained spectral coordinates are nonzero. Let Splus be ALL retained nodes with Q(lambda)=H (not merely the union of limiting positive-weight supports). Off Splus, weights are summable. Those with |Q|<H are exponentially small, while the only remaining external nodes satisfy Q(beta)=-H.

## Already proved

1. If |Splus|<=4 then the limiting weights are unique from the three q-orthogonality equations and normalization, hence convergence.

2. If q=r, convergence for every dimension follows from agent2_equal_limit_polynomials.md. BV-tail distance of q_k from q is O(H-h_k), while the projection identity makes it quadratic in that distance plus exponentially small external weights; absorption gives exponential convergence.

3. If deg gcd(q,r)=2, convergence for every dimension follows from agent3_s3_gcd2_lemma.md, independently audited by agent1 (#267). The quadratic normal polynomial is D*c+O(D^2+eta), so persistent residues have fixed signs modulo summable wrong-sign parts.

4. If there are NO negative-level external nodes, all external weights decay exponentially. Project onto the at-most-six core nodes. Exact core pole recurrences plus exponentially small perturbations prove convergence, as follows.
   - Five-node core: a is monic quadratic and t=h(z-zeta). The scalar residue R=zeta-eta satisfies R_next=C R, C->1 positive, by the constant-B determinant identity. Exponentially small errors are handled by the scalar integrating-factor lemma.
   - Six-node core: a and t/h are monic quadratics. Each residue has the exact recurrence R_j,next=C_j R_j-D_j K, with C_j->1 positive, D_1>0 and D_2<0; K=h_next-h>=0. The same integrating-factor lemma gives eventual sign or an exponentially small wrong-sign part. B-compression/interlacing gives the nonnegative bounded new-pole coefficient, so both poles converge.
   See agent2_B_compression_proof.md and the team's exact pole recurrences.

## Entropies for negative external nodes

For a full simple six-node core lambda1<...<lambda6, let ell_i be its Lagrange interpolation polynomials. For Q(beta)=-H,

    L_beta=log w_beta + sum_i ell_i(beta) log w_i

is eventually strictly increasing, with increment at least c(H-h_k). BV-tail control makes every Taylor remainder O((H-h_k)^2), whereas the leading term is positive of order H-h_k. If beta is in band B_j=(lambda_{2j-1},lambda_{2j}), its negative core coefficients are:

    B1: i=3,5;     B2: i=2,5;     B3: i=2,4.

Thus any negative external node forces the omega-limit set onto a proper union of two adjacent edges of the fixed square. Negative external nodes cannot occupy all three bands (positive Stieltjes/entropy-cone certificate, agent1 #198).

### Two occupied outer bands: convergence is proved

Suppose beta in B1 and gamma in B3. Let xi=lambda3 or lambda4 and take positive a,b with

    a/(z-beta)+b/(z-gamma)=(z-xi)/((z-beta)(z-gamma)).

Then c_i=a ell_i(beta)+b ell_i(gamma) equals

    2H(lambda_i-xi)/[(lambda_i-beta)(lambda_i-gamma)P'(lambda_i)].

For xi=lambda3, all c_i are nonnegative except c_4<0 (c_3=0). Monotonicity of aL_beta+bL_gamma and w_beta,w_gamma->0 therefore force w_4->0. Choosing xi=lambda4 forces w_3->0. Only four core nodes remain, so the limiting weights are unique. An exact algebraic instance of both certificates is checked in agent3_s3_entropy_middle_check.py.

### One occupied middle band: convergence is proved by extremal poles

If negative external nodes occur only in B2, the two persistent Dirichlet poles are respectively the leftmost and rightmost non-exponentially-decaying t-poles. At a zero residue, B has that pole as a root; interlacing with the next t polynomial makes residue crossings one-way. Regularity holds for gcd<=1, while gcd2 is handled independently above. The one-sided scalar integrating-factor argument, with exponentially small discarded modes, then gives convergence of both poles.

### Outer empty band: exact remaining geometry

Suppose the only possible occupied bands are B1,B2 and B3 is empty. A positive two-node Stieltjes certificate with numerator z-lambda2 or z-lambda3 has all nonnegative core coefficients except c5<0. Therefore w5->0, confining the omega-limit set to the fixed edge w5=0. The right persistent pole tends lambda5 and has bounded variation by its extremal-pole barrier. If only B1 is occupied, the same conclusion is needed only when that extremal pole tends its outward endpoint lambda5; other limiting positions force the second pole to an endpoint via the single entropy and yield convergence directly. The reflected configuration is identical.

On the edge, let u be the remaining persistent pole, let g=w5, and let R1,R2 be the two residues. Put D=H-h. The proved BV estimate gives |R_j|<=C D. Analytic-ideal factorization yields, for the exact six-node core,

    R1,next = a_k R1 - g R2^2 B_k,       B_k>=0,

after absorbing terms divisible by R1 into a_k. Negative external nodes add signed linear forcing: the far band B1 has positive coefficient and the nearer B2 negative coefficient. On every compact OPEN edge segment, entropy comparison shows the near-band mass is a higher power of the far-band mass, hence is negligible. The ghost forcing gR2^2 has tail o(D), because g is comparable to the outward pole's remaining distance and that pole is monotone.

The team has established pole-energy and residue-BV lemmas (agent2_pole_residue_BV_lemma.md), and bounded homogeneous transport on compact open edge segments. A tail-energy absorption would close convergence if far-band dominance were uniform for the entire future orbit.

## Precise unresolved point

The entropy dominance is NOT uniform near the endpoint where another core weight vanishes: a logarithmic term can diverge and permit the near external band to revive. Also off-face transport has a possible boundary-layer g/(u-endpoint) term. Therefore the current work does NOT yet exclude infinitely many edge excursions with deep vertex visits. One needs a local no-return/energy argument across such visits, or a globally uniform corrected transport/entropy invariant. No assertion of a complete s=3 proof is made here.

The case |Splus|=5 can be regarded as an edge with the sixth positive-level root a permanently zero virtual coordinate when that root is distinct. If Q-H has a double positive-level root, one must explicitly use the confluent-factor version (or remain in the five-node a/t formulation); this should not be silently omitted.

This lemma is rigorous but conditional. Its application to the whole closed s=3 edge has NOT been established: uniform scalar transport at a two-facet corner and the global one-sided sign of the combined negative-action forcing remain open.

Let D_k>0 decrease to zero. Let u_k be bounded, R_k real, and A_k positive with c<=A_k<=C. Set z_k=R_k/A_k. Assume the following, for all sufficiently large k.

(1) |z_k|<=C D_k, and z_{k+1}-z_k=P_k-Q_k+epsilon_k, where P,Q are nonnegative summable sequences and sum_{i>=k}|epsilon_i|=o(D_k).

(2) There is a bounded scalar sequence Phi_k and a real sequence e_k=o(D_k) such that the tail series exists and

 D_k <= C_0 [ sum_{i>=k} z_i(Phi_{i+1}-Phi_i) + sum_{i>=k}P_i ] + e_k.

(3) sum_{i>=k}Q_i=o(D_k).

 <= 4B[Q[k]+E[k]].

A bounded real sequence with summable positive increments converges: write the positive and negative Jordan variations, and use boundedness to show the latter is finite. QED.

D=H-h; u=free Dirichlet pole; R=its residue; A=bounded homogeneous transport; P=far-band negative action after domination; Q=positive-ghost forcing, comparable to g S^2; Phi=a bounded primitive of the averaged energy coefficient after transport.  sum_{i>=k}g_i S_i^2

### experiments/e4/agent2_s2_all_n_proof.md 
 # Complete convergence proof for s=2, arbitrary finite dimension

This proof uses the team's established global BV lemma: after discarding the finite initial segment before the last support deletion, all retained spectral weights are positive; h_k=E_w q_k^2 increases to H>0; consecutive monic quadratics converge by parity to q,r and obey ||q_k-q_parity||<=C(H-h_k); F=qr equals H on every omega-limit support; every retained initial node satisfies |F(lambda)|<=H. Nodes with |F|<H have exponentially decreasing weights, and nodes with F=-H have weights tending to zero (indeed summably). The even residual sequence is asymptotically regular.

Let U be the union of the supports of all even cluster measures, and let S be the retained initial nodes with F=H. Then U is contained in S and |S|<=4. If |U|<=3, every even cluster measure is uniquely determined by q-orthogonality and total mass on U. For three nodes, q(lambda_i)w_i is the one-dimensional null vector of the two-row Vandermonde matrix, and positivity and normalization fix its scale; q cannot vanish at a supporting node. Measures with fewer than three nodes have h_2=0 and cannot be limiting measures. Thus the even weights converge in this case.

Henceforth assume |U|=4, so U=S. Write its nodes lambda1<lambda2<lambda3<lambda4. Put P0(z)=prod_i(z-lambdai); then F=P0+H. Each of q,r has one root in each band (lambda1,lambda2),(lambda3,lambda4), and both are strictly negative throughout the closed central gap [lambda2,lambda3]. This follows from positivity and the degree-two orthogonality, or from the sign alternation in its Vandermonde null vector. Every other retained node is in one of these two bands, since |F|<=H implies -2H<=P0<=0.

## 1. A negative-neutral external node forces loss of one core node

Let ell_i be the cubic Lagrange basis on S. For a node beta with F(beta)=-H define
 L_beta(k)=log w_{k,beta}+sum_i ell_i(beta)log w_{k,i}.
All these weights are positive. Write F_k=q_k q_{k+1} and D_k=H-h_k. The exact two-block update gives
 L_beta(k+2)-L_beta(k)
 =2[log|F_k(beta)|+sum_i ell_i(beta)log F_k(lambdai)]-2log(h_k h_{k+1}).
The BV tail bound gives ||F_k-F||<=C D_k. Its degree is at most three. Taylor expansion and Lagrange interpolation therefore cancel all linear terms:
 Delta L_beta=-2log(h_k h_{k+1}/H^2)+O(D_k^2)>=D_k/H>=0
eventually. (If D_k=0, the orbit already has T^2y=y.)

If beta lies in the left band, ell_1(beta),ell_2(beta),ell_4(beta)>0 and ell_3(beta)<0. Therefore
 L_beta(k)<=log w_{k,beta}+ell_3(beta)log w_{k,3}.
The left side is eventually bounded below, and log w_{k,beta}->-infinity. Consequently w_{k,3}->0. If beta is in the right band, the same argument forces w_{k,2}->0, since only ell_2(beta) is negative there. Thus the presence of any negative-neutral external node reduces the actual limiting support to at most three nodes, and the previous Vandermonde uniqueness argument proves convergence.

It remains to consider the case with no negative-neutral nodes. Then every node outside S has exponentially decreasing weight.

First consider an exact four-node weight step. Let M=P0 sum_i w_i/(z-lambdai) be its monic cubic Stieltjes numerator. Divide
 q_w M=(z-eta)P0+h(z-zeta),
where q_w is the monic orthogonal quadratic and h=E_w q_w^2. The restart identity is
 M_next=q_w(z-zeta).
Put primes on next-step quantities, K=h'-h>=0 and R=zeta-eta. Polynomial elimination gives
 h'(z-zeta')(z-eta)-h(z-eta')(z-zeta)=K q_w(z),
 K[h q_w(zeta)+q_w(eta)P0(zeta)]=-h R^2 P0(zeta),
 R'-R=(K/R)[q_w(eta)/h-q_w(zeta)/h'].
The last formula extends continuously to R=0. Near the compact limiting two-cycle set, the denominator in the second identity tends to q(zeta)^2 r(zeta), or r(zeta)^2 q(zeta), and is bounded away from zero. Consequently K=R^2 C0(w), with C0 bounded analytic. In the third identity the bracket is O(R)+O(K), so
 R'=R+R^2 A(w),
where A is uniformly bounded. This conclusion does not require R to be a regular coordinate and remains valid when q=r.

There is a second useful exact identity. Evaluate q_next M_next=(z-eta')P0+h'(z-zeta') at zeta', using M_next=q_w(z-zeta):
 zeta'-zeta=R' C(w),
 C(w)=P0(zeta')/[q_w(zeta')q_next(zeta')].
For sufficiently late steps, q_w and q_next are negative throughout the central gap, and zeta' lies in that gap. Thus 0<=C(w)<=C uniformly.

## 3. Exponentially perturbed four-node orbits

Project the original weights onto S and renormalize. Their exact update differs from the four-node map by O(rho^k), rho<1. The monic moment Gram matrix stays uniformly positive definite, since limiting supports contain at least three distinct nodes, and h is bounded below. The quantities eta,zeta,R are smooth functions of the four weights near the compact limiting set. Thus, for the projected sequence,
 R_{k+1}=a_k R_k+epsilon_k,
 a_k=1+O(R_k)->1, |epsilon_k|<=C rho^k,
and
 zeta_{k+1}-zeta_k=C_k R_{k+1}+delta_k,
 0<=C_k<=C, |delta_k|<=C rho^k.
Here R_k->0, since every cluster measure is a two-cycle and its Stieltjes numerator has the form r(z-zeta), or q(z-zeta), making eta=zeta.

For completeness, the elementary scalar perturbation argument is as follows. Choose K so a_k>0 thereafter and put A_K=1,A_{k+1}=a_k A_k. Then A_k=exp(o(k)), and
 u_k=R_k/A_k
has exponentially summable increments epsilon_k/A_{k+1}; hence u_k converges. If its limit is nonzero, R_k has eventually constant sign. If its limit is zero, then
 |R_k|<=A_k sum_{j>=k}|epsilon_j|/A_{j+1}<=C sigma^k
for some sigma<1. The latter estimate follows by bounding a_j between 1-delta and 1+delta, with delta sufficiently small relative to rho.

If R eventually has constant sign, the pole's variation in the opposite direction is exponentially summable. If R decays exponentially, its entire pole variation is summable. Since zeta is bounded, it converges in either case.

All even cluster measures now have the same Stieltjes numerator r(z-zeta_infinity) on S, hence the same weights. The even spectral weights converge. At each persistent spectral component the signed normalized two-step multiplier tends to F(lambda)/H=1; its sign is therefore eventually constant. All other components vanish. This proves Euclidean convergence of y_{2k} for arbitrary n when s=2.

Exact identities are checked in agent2_s2_pole_checks.py. The interpolation cancellation and Lagrange sign certificates are checked in agent2_s2_entropy_checks.py. The argument relies only on those identities and the independently proved global BV lemma.
